title: BDS-Lite: code and evidence for "When does boundary distillation help lightweight medical image segmentation?"
description:
Code, configurations, split manifests, study protocols, frozen analysis outputs, evidence archives and manuscript sources for J. Chen, C. Hong, Y. Wu, T. Yang, When does boundary distillation help lightweight medical image segmentation? (PeerJ Computer Science, manuscript CS-2026:06:142937, revised version).

This is a single-commit snapshot without development history; the README explains what is not included and how frozen files are verified with SHA-256 digests and OpenTimestamps proofs.

The original code and text are licensed under the MIT License. Third-party material keeps its own terms and is not covered by the MIT License: the ACDC images in Figure 3 of the manuscript (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; cite Bernard et al., IEEE TMI 2018), the ISIC 2018 Task 1 reference masks drawn in the contour figures (CC0), and adapted third-party code (Apache-2.0 and MIT). See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/ in the archive.
notes: Third-party image licences (Figure 3: ACDC, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; ISIC 2018 reference masks: CC0) and third-party code licences are listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; they are not covered by the MIT License of the code.
